title: Selective-Opening Security for Compactly Committing AEAD
summary: Existing committing-AEAD definitions omit selective-opening attacks, and it remains open whether compact commitment can coexist with selective-opening security.

formal_statement.body: Existing committing-$\mathrm{AEAD}$ definitions do not model selective-opening attacks, which may permit compromise of the entire cryptographic key rather than only access to commitment openings. Determine whether compact commitment and selective-opening security are compatible: construct a compactly committing $\mathrm{AEAD}$ scheme and prove it secure against selective-opening attacks, at least in the random-oracle model, or establish a fundamental incompatibility between committing $\mathrm{AEAD}$ and selective-opening security.

scope.domain: Symmetric authenticated encryption research on committing AEAD and security against selective-opening attacks.
parameters: compactly committing AEAD scheme: target construction
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether compact commitment and selective-opening security are compatible by constructing and proving secure a compactly committing AEAD scheme, at least in the random-oracle model, or by establishing a fundamental incompatibility.

citations.label: Message Franking via Committing Authenticated Encryption

progress.summary: The source presents this as a future direction and explicitly conjectures that the apparent tension is not fundamental. It calls for a selectively opening secure compactly committing AEAD construction, particularly in the random-oracle model.
